title: Exception-aware rule application wired into brain.reason's one production entry point
goal: Close the gap EXP-083/085 both named as a follow-up: the exception-aware multi-exception OR-combination mechanism they proved standalone was never reachable from lab.common.brain.reason, the single entry point every other capability in this repo goes through. Wire it into reason()'s existing verb-rule branch and prove all three of its honest states (unresolved -> flagged; holds -> suppressed; ruled out -> clean) are reachable by passing plain passages through reason() alone, not by calling forward_chain directly.
method: lab.common.brain.reason's existing `if applied['matched']:` branch (verb-trigger rule shape) now calls lab.common.inference.split_exceptions/check_exceptions (both unchanged, proven in EXP-085) against every other given passage as context before asserting the rule's consequence. decision='supported_with_flags' (already used by the longform cross-page-contradiction path) is reused for an unresolved exception; a held exception suppresses the consequence and returns an explanatory line instead, the same pattern the existing threshold-rule role-mismatch branch already used. Three cases, same rule/fact fixture as EXP-085, run through reason(ask, passages) directly.

case1_no_context.text: MedCorp processed Aisha. [fact-1] matches the rule's trigger (process): If anyone processes special category data, it is unlawful, unless the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes; processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person where the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent; or processing is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims or whenever courts are acting in their judicial capacity. [rule-1] Therefore, it is unlawful, unless the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes; processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person where the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent; or processing is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims or whenever courts are acting in their judicial capacity (the rule's exception is unresolved -- not confirmed either way)..

case2_exception_holds.text: policy does not apply: the rule's exception holds ('If anyone processes special category data, it is unlawful, unless the data subject has given explicit consent to the processing of those personal data for one or more specified purposes; processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person where the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent; or processing is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims or whenever courts are acting in their judicial capacity.') [rule-1].

conclusion: The exception-aware rule-application path is now reachable from lab.common.brain.reason itself, not only from a standalone forward_chain call: an unresolved exception derives the consequence but flags the overall decision (supported_with_flags), a confirmed exception suppresses the consequence entirely and returns an explanatory non-applicability line instead of asserting it, and a confidently ruled-out exception derives cleanly with no flag -- all three reachable by passing plain passages through the one entry point every other capability already goes through, with no hand-assembled call sequence.
scale_down: Only the verb-trigger rule shape (parse_conditional_rule) is wired -- the threshold-rule branch (parse_threshold_rule/apply_threshold_rule) does not go through split_exceptions/check_exceptions at all and is unaffected by this exploration, a real and separate gap if a threshold rule's own consequence ever carries an 'unless' clause. Three hand-built cases through reason(), not a broad test across many rule/passage combinations.
follow_ups: The threshold-rule branch (apply_threshold_rule) still has no exception awareness at all -- a separate, smaller follow-up if a threshold rule's consequence is ever found with an 'unless' clause in a real document.
Not tested combined with the other reason() signals (identity/total/document) firing at the same time as the rule branch on the same ask -- only the rule branch's own behavior was exercised here.
models_used: Same as EXP-083/085: spaCy dependency parser (unchanged) + MoritzLaurer/DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli via the existing, unmodified check_exception/check_exceptions. No generative model, no new dependency -- this exploration only wires existing, already-measured pieces into reason().
